result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers put a visible search field up front and handle typing and zero results well, including filter-caused empties, spelling fixes, purchase and interlibrary-loan requests, and errors kept separate from empty results. A explains more clearly which tabs to keep and which to demote, and its Home 'needs attention' strip is a strong touch. B is more thorough about what the app remembers (sort and filters, last pickup branch, scroll position, event filters) and gives concrete behavior for every screen. That puts B slightly ahead overall. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers lay out usable screens, with strong typing behavior and good zero-result handling (filter relaxation with counts, spelling correction, purchase suggestion or interlibrary loan, and offline errors kept separate from empty results). A is stronger on what the app remembers (pickup branch, filters, event chips, back position) and has a cleaner search-first structure. B gives clearer reasons for what goes in the bar versus More, and adds a Home 'needs attention' strip and quick card access, though its separate Home and Search tabs partly overlap.
